title: 22‑Year‑Old Confesses to Milestone Bitcoin Theft
subtitle: Malone Lam admits involvement in scheme that diverted millions in cryptocurrencies
excerpt: A 22‑year‑old man pleaded guilty to participating in a scheme that stole hundreds of millions of dollars in bitcoin in the United States.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
A 22‑year‑old man pleaded guilty to participating in a criminal conspiracy to steal hundreds of millions of dollars in bitcoin from a Washington, D.C., resident. The investigation revealed that the group used social‑engineering techniques and the diverted funds financed a life of luxury with sports cars and mansions.

The Defendant’s Guilty Plea

Malone Lam, 22, from Singapore, appeared in court and pleaded guilty to a charge of conspiracy to extort. The defendant admitted before District Judge Colleen Kollar‑Kotelly that he organized a network of young people who carried out a series of cryptocurrency scams. With the confession, the case marks a significant advance for the U.S. Department of Justice investigation.

How the Bitcoin Scam Worked

The prosecutors detailed how the group used techniques to deceive victims and gain access to cryptocurrency funds. In one episode, co‑conspirators posed as representatives of Google and a cryptocurrency brokerage to manipulate a Washington resident into revealing security codes. With that data, the criminals were able to transfer more than four thousand bitcoins, worth over $240 million.

Extravagant Spending on Stolen Money

Authorities point out that the proceeds from the stolen cryptocurrency were converted into cash and used for a series of extravagant purchases. Lam financed a fleet of sports cars, rented mansions in Miami, and spent large sums on nightclubs. Among the assets acquired were high‑value watches and dozens of vehicles from brands such as Porsche, Lamborghini, and Ferrari.

Arrest and Next Legal Steps

After a period of intense spending, Lam was arrested by FBI agents at his rented Miami home. The defendant faces a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison, as well as possible deportation. The judge handling the case did not schedule a sentencing hearing immediately, but set a status hearing for the proceeding.

With information from CNN, WPEC, Courthouse News.
